finding_key: packages/backend/src/datasource/datasource.service.ts::raw-text oid guard is bypassed for array/range date-time types, so the timezone-shift bug it fixes still occurs for `timestamp[]`, `date[]`, `timestamptz[]`, `tsrange`, `tstzrange`

verdict.reasoning: RAW_TEXT_OIDS at packages/backend/src/datasource/datasource.service.ts:20-24 lists only the scalar 1082/1114/1184 OIDs, and datasourceTypeParser (lines 34-37) sends every other OID to the pg-types default, which registers parseDateArray for 1115 (_timestamp), 1182 (_date) and 1185 (_timestamptz) — so array date/time columns still come back as JS Date built from the Node runtime timezone, and `SET TimeZone = 'UTC'` only changes server-side text rendering, not the offset-less client-side parse. Those arrays hit the object branch of toCell (packages/sheets/src/store/readonly.ts:31-35) and JSON.stringify serializes the Dates as shifted ISO strings, and the new type matrix in packages/backend/test/database.e2e-spec.ts covers scalars only, so nothing catches it. The claim overreaches on ranges: pg-types registers no parser for tsrange/tstzrange (3908/3910), so those stay raw strings and are unaffected — but the array gap, which is the substance of the finding, is real. Severity is minor because only array-typed date/time result columns are affected; confidence is medium since no checkout was mounted to pin the installed pg-types parser table.
